newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek uranium output seen nearly double by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek uranium output seen nearly double by 1999.

text.p: Uzbekistan, seeing strengthened demand for uranium on international markets, plans to boost annual uranium output to 3,000 tonnes by 1999 from 1,700 tonnes in 1996, an Uzbek mining official said on Friday.

"Our enterprise will take advantage of the rise in world prices for uranium which is used in nuclear power plants," Yevgeny Tolstov, chief engineer at the Navoi mining and metallurgical plant, told Reuters.
"This allows us to increase uranium output to 2,400 tonnes next year (1998) and 3,000 tonnes in 1999," he said.
The Navoi plant is the former Soviet republic's only producer of enriched uranium, used as fuel in nuclear power stations.
Tolstov said in Soviet times, Uzbekistan's uranium output peaked at 3,500 tonnes a year but plunged to 2,000 tonnes in 1995 and 1,700 tonnes in 1996.
Tolstov said the United States had increased the quota for uranium imports from Uzbekistan at the end of last year but gave no further details.
He said Uzbekistan has 27 uranium fields with proven reserves of 55,000 tonnes.
Observers say that up until the 1996 fall in Uzbek uranium output, the Central Asian state was the world's third largest uranium exporter and its fifth largest producer.
